subject: Literature
title: The Harlem Renaissance
description: A quick, practical guide to The Harlem Renaissance.

hook.text: In the 1920s, Harlem became the center of a Black cultural explosion in literature, music, and art.

buildup.text: Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, and Claude McKay wrote poetry and fiction celebrating Black identity.

discovery.text: Hughes declared he would write about Black life honestly, without shame or apology, in his own voice.

twist.text: Some Black intellectuals criticized the movement for portraying folk culture instead of middle-class respectability.

climax.text: The Harlem Renaissance created a literary tradition that shaped the civil rights movement and modern Black writing.

punchline.text: A neighborhood's poetry became a nation's conscience.

quiz.question: What was Langston Hughes's approach to writing?
options: He wrote about Black life honestly, without shame or apology
He focused exclusively on political speeches
